shorts.title: What you will learn: unique_ptr
shorts.script: A pointer that frees itself. Today we meet the smart pointer that you will use most. It owns a heap object, and it frees the object for you. A unique pointer owns one heap object. When the unique pointer dies, it deletes the object. You never write delete. This is RAII for heap memory. A unique pointer has one owner. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: unique_ptr.

shorts.title: unique_ptr in one minute
shorts.hook: A unique pointer owns one heap object.
shorts.script: A unique pointer owns one heap object. When the unique pointer dies, it deletes the object. You never write delete. This is RAII for heap memory. A unique pointer has one owner. You cannot copy it, but you can move it to a new owner. Think of a house key with one owner. You can hand it over, but you cannot copy it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: unique_ptr in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: A owns an int with the value five.
shorts.script: A owns an int with the value five. Move hands the ownership to b. A is now empty. It equals nullptr, so the program prints one. B owns the int and reads five. When b dies, the int is deleted exactly once. The program prints one, and then five. A unique pointer owns one heap object. It deletes the object when it dies. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Copying a unique_ptr
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in unique pointers?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in unique pointers? Bug of the Day. We copy a unique pointer. The compiler says use of deleted function. The copy is blocked on purpose. Two owners would delete the object twice. Use move to hand over the ownership. Two unique pointers must never own the same object, or it would be deleted twice. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Copying a unique_ptr.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you own a heap int in unique pointers?
shorts.script: Can you own a heap int in unique pointers? A unique pointer never shares its umbrella. It is all about ownership. Make a unique pointer to an int with the value twenty. Add one through the pointer, and print the result. Write your answer in the comments. A unique pointer owns one heap object. It deletes the object when it dies. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
